corrections.before: "Soul Crystal" V1.5, written from 1989 to 1992 by Avantgardistic Arts. (C) 1992 by Avantgardistic Arts, Hannover & Starbyte Software, Bochum. This adventure has 103 locations, more than 130 high-resolution color graphics, approximately 320 Kbytes of text and an approximately 30-minute soundtrack. This program development took a total of 16 so-called "man-years". So please be so fair and "spread the word - not the disk!" But if this is a pirated copy (even though the program was protected, and certainly not without reason...), then please think about the ASDG philosophy "A program worth using is a program worth buying" - alone Even the original packaging and the manuals should be worth the money to you. Have fun playing "Soul Crystal", and - oh yes: As far as we know, this is the first adventure in which a CHEATMODE hasbeen implemented - so you should make an effort to find it...
corrections.after: "Soul Crystal" V1.5, written from 1989 to 1992 by Avantgardistic Arts. (C) 1992 by Avantgardistic Arts, Hannover & Starbyte Software, Bochum. This adventure contains 103 locations, more than 130 high-resolution colour pictures, about 320 KBytes of text and roughly half an hour of music. Development took a total of 16 person-years. So please play fair: "spread the word - not the disk!" If this is a pirated copy after all (despite the copy protection, which was there for a reason...), spare a thought for ASDG's motto: "A program worth using is a program worth buying". The original box and manuals alone should be worth the money. Have fun playing "Soul Crystal"! Oh, and as far as we know, this is the first adventure with a built-in CHEATMODE. Better start looking...

corrections.before: Please insert the diskette to be initialized into your floppy drive. Please keep in mind, however, that any data that may have been on it will be irretrievably lost during the formatting process! corrections.after: Insert the disk you want to initialise into your floppy drive. Make sure it is not write-protected, or the operation may fail! Any other action cancels it.

corrections.before: Mylgor's amulet is made of an unfamiliar metal, and as you pick it up it begins to pulse slightly, as if it were alive with its own life! You can hardly concentrate anymore - everything around you starts to blur! You stagger - and fall! The shock makes you lose the amulet: It rolls over the ground and out of your eyes - but its hypnotizing effect is finally broken! Dazed, you get up again, look for the amulet and pick it up again with trembling fingers, being careful not to fall under the spell again...
corrections.after: Mylgor's amulet is made of a metal you don't recognise. As you pick it up, it begins to pulse gently, as though it has a life of its own. You gaze at the glowing green snake on its surface and notice it moving slightly, twisting its body into one variation of the letter "Z" after another. You can barely concentrate. Everything around you blurs! You stagger, then fall! The shock makes you drop the amulet. It rolls away out of sight, but at last its hypnotic spell is broken. Dazed, you get up, find it and pick it up with trembling fingers, taking care not to fall under its spell again...
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.after: You carefully open it. A few seconds later, it occurs to you that you couldn't possibly have opened it in the first place! So you close it again, leave everything as it was and resolve never to think about logic in computer programs again.

corrections.before: You clumsily step into the thick fur boots that Mylgor gave you. Man, are they warm! Better not to take them off again indoors...
corrections.after: You clumsily pull on the thick fur boots Mylgor gave you. Boy, are they warm! Best not take them off indoors...

corrections.before: Carefully you puff on the orc father's whistle. Her sweet smoke transports you to another world: a world where you fly through the clouds on a lowered toaster, where pink elephants direct the traffic. Suddenly it starts raining colorful raindrops - and the visibility in your turbo toaster is getting worse and worse, because the windshield wipers are of course on strike again! Such a crap! You were with the box but only just at the Toaster Monitoring Association (TÜV)! bang! Now it's happened again: as soon as you're not paying attention for a while, one of those jaded marzipan potato riders takes the right of way! "It was his fault!" You still think to yourself as you smash your turnip through the windshield. Then the lights go out... When you come to, you're back where you puffed the whistle - but you've got a terrible headache. Man! what a herb...
corrections.after: You cautiously take a puff on the orc father's pipe. Its sweet smoke carries you into another world, where you fly through the clouds in a customised, low-slung toaster and pink elephants direct the traffic. Suddenly, multicoloured raindrops start falling. Visibility in your turbo-toaster gets worse and worse, because naturally the windscreen wipers have packed up again! Damn it! You only just had the thing inspected by the Toaster Testing Authority! CRUNCH! There we go again. Look away for one second and some stuck-up marzipan-potato jockey cuts you off! "His fault!" you think as your head goes through the windscreen. Then the lights go out... When you come round, you're back where you took that puff, with a truly thunderous headache. Man! What was IN that stuff?
corrections.reason: Pfeife is pipe; idioms include lowered/custom toaster, vehicle testing pun, losing right of way and head, not turnip.

corrections.before: Well, whatever you say: heroically you throw yourself into the blade of your sword - but nothing happens! No blood, no pain, absolutely nothing! Frustrated, you make another attempt, but again you feel nothing. The third time you finally meet: In agony you writhe on the floor without a word of pain passing your lips - as it should be for a real hero. If only your girlfriend could see that! After all, it's not every day that you make such a stylish exit! Suddenly it's all over and it's getting dark... After a while you wake up floating in a dark room. You shudder: Is this life after death? Is that really all? It looks dark... But suddenly you realize what woke you up: Quietly, as if from far away, a soft voice blows over to you... "Dave Parker!" You can hear her whispering, "You you should know that no one can escape his destiny! There is no point in fleeing his destiny - destiny always catches up with you! So go and fulfill the tasks that have been given to you. By the power of my divine powers, I will be thee now give you an extra life to give you one more opportunity to fulfill your destiny..." As the voice fades away into nothing, everything around you begins to spin, you become dizzy - and you fall into a deep, dreamless sleep ... When you open your eyes again, you find yourself exactly where you attempted suicide...
corrections.after: All right, have it your way. Heroically, you throw yourself onto your sword. Nothing happens! No blood, no pain, absolutely nothing! Frustrated, you try again. Still nothing. On your third attempt, you finally hit the target: yourself. You writhe on the ground in your death throes, without so much as a cry of pain. A true hero to the last! If only your girlfriend could see you now. You don't make an exit this stylish every day! Then it is over, and everything goes dark... Some time later, you wake to find yourself floating in a dark space. You shudder. Is this the afterlife? Is this really all there is? Not a bright prospect... Then you realise what woke you. A gentle voice drifts towards you, faint and distant. "Dave Parker!" it whispers. "You should know that no one can escape their destiny. Fleeing it is pointless: fate always catches up with you! Go and complete the tasks you have been given. By my divine authority, I grant you an extra life, and one more chance to fulfil your destiny..." As the voice fades, everything starts spinning. You grow dizzy and fall into a deep, dreamless sleep. When you open your eyes again, you are exactly where you tried to kill yourself...
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: You are now wearing lined, warm pants.
corrections.after: You are now wearing the warm, lined trousers.
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: Unfortunately, it's too hard to lie comfortably on it - and also: It's not fun to do it so quickly...
corrections.after: It's too hard to lie on comfortably. Besides, rushing things takes all the fun out of it...

corrections.before: You are in your small but, considering its price, quite comfortably furnished hotel room. You wake up from your admiration when you suddenly remember that you had actually promised to call home after your arrival, but in view of all these new impressions your mother will probably be able to wait a little longer.
corrections.after: Your hotel room is small, but quite cosy for the price. Against the west wall stands a wardrobe decorated with elaborate folk-art paintings. Through the window to the west, you can watch the sun setting behind the mountains around Loch Calderwood, bathing the evening landscape in a warm golden glow. corrections.after: [Outside Mylgor's house]

corrections.before: This is the lobby of "Mary's Inn", where you will be staying for the next few days and weeks. You can see a street through the door in the east wall and the reception through the northern wall opening. It seems to be pretty quiet at the moment though, and somehow the sight of this lonely and deserted space makes you a little depressed. But whatever? Maybe more visitors will come tomorrow at breakfast time. As you look around you can't help but get the impression that the people who set up this space were keen to express the prosperity and cosmopolitanism of their village. Unfortunately, this spasmodic attempt has failed completely: The result of their efforts reminds you much more of the hotel foyers in American soap operas - with the insignificant difference that these are about five times larger! Nevertheless: at least the landscape is fantastic, and after all that's why you came here!
corrections.after: This is the lobby of "Mary's Inn", your home for the next few weeks. A door in the east wall opens onto the street; an opening to the north leads to reception. The place is deserted, and the emptiness is rather depressing. Still, perhaps things will pick up at breakfast tomorrow. Looking around, you get the impression the decorators were desperate to show how prosperous and worldly their little village is. Sadly, they tried rather too hard. The result reminds you of the hotel lobbies in American soap operas, with one tiny difference: those are about five times bigger! Never mind. At least the scenery is fantastic, and that's what you came for, isn't it?
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: You are standing on the road that leads from "Mary's Inn", your hotel, to Loch Calderwood. You feel the warmth of the evening sun on your skin and listen to the birds singing their goodnight songs on the trees that line the roadside rustling in the gentle wind. The first vacation that you have traveled alone is actually starting to be quite good, you think to yourself, and resolve to enjoy this vacation as much as possible. On your left, to the west, is the entrance to Mary's Inn, while the road stretches east. On the right side of the road there is an advertising sign that reads: "Last hotel before the next system crash!"
corrections.after: You are on the road from "Mary's Inn" to Loch Calderwood. The evening sun warms your skin, and birds sing their goodnight songs in the roadside trees, which rustle in the gentle breeze. Your first holiday on your own is off to a pretty good start. You intend to enjoy every minute of it! The entrance to "Mary's Inn" is on your left, to the west, while the road continues east. A sign on the right reads: "Last hotel before the next system crash!"
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: You walk down a lonely, dusty road that leads from your hotel to the shores of Loch Calderwood. Despite the late evening hour, it is still pleasantly warm: the ground radiates all the heat that it has stored throughout the whole sunny day. You feel a little exhausted and think of your parched throat that you wish you could lubricate with a nice tankard of ice cold beer, but then again just a little further north is the mountain lake where you wanted to cool your smoking feet. But if you decide to have a drink at the hotel bar, you can of course walk back west along the street.
corrections.after: You stroll along the lonely, dusty road from your hotel to Loch Calderwood. It's getting late, but the ground still gives off the heat it soaked up all day. You're a little tired, and your parched throat could do with a tankard of ice-cold beer. On the other hand, the mountain lake is just a little farther north, and you did want to cool those steaming feet. If a drink at the hotel bar sounds more tempting, you can follow the road back west.
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: You're standing in a short, clean corridor with white-painted walls and thick, red carpets on the polished parquet floor. A few doors, painted black and numbered gold, lead to the guest rooms. Your own room faces south, and since you're unlikely to get your hands on the keys to the other rooms, your only alternative is to break through the wall in the east wall, behind which you can see the reception.
corrections.after: You are in a short, clean corridor with white walls and thick red carpets over polished parquet. Black doors with gold number plates lead to the guest rooms. Your room is to the south. Since you're unlikely to get hold of the keys to the other rooms, your only alternative is the opening in the east wall, which leads to reception.
corrections.reason: Wanddurchbruch is an existing opening, not an instruction to break through a wall.

corrections.before: You are standing at the reception of your hotel. Directly in front of you is the massive reception desk, behind which you can see a key board. When you take a closer look, you realize that you are probably the only guest in the hotel at the moment: Almost all the room keys are still on the board! Further to the right you can see some mailboxes, but all of them are empty. Well, at least your mother will write to you - and if it's just a reminder that you always go to bed on time, change your socks every day and take your vitamin pills!
corrections.after: You are at the hotel reception desk. Behind the massive counter is a key board. Almost all the keys are still hanging there, so you're probably the only guest! Farther right are some pigeonholes, all empty. Well, at least Mum will write. Even if it's only to remind you to go to bed on time, change your socks every day and take your vitamin pills!
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: As you slowly drift south, you notice that the current is getting stronger - until you realize the danger you are in! You try with all your might to swim against the pull, but it's already too late: thrashing wildly around you are pulled down by a mighty whirlpool to the bottom of the mountain lake, where you die an agonizing death... At the moment of your death you believe below you you can still see the golden domes of the old sunken city the locals used to tell you about, but given the unfortunate situation you've gotten yourself into, it really is highly unlikely that you'll ever get a chance to hear their rumors again to confirm: you don't even have time for one last prayer...
corrections.after: As you drift south, the current grows stronger and stronger. Suddenly you realise the danger! You swim desperately against the pull, but it's too late. A vast whirlpool drags you, thrashing, to the bottom of the mountain lake, where you drown in agony... In your final moments, you think you glimpse the golden domes of the sunken city the locals told you about. Unfortunately, given your present circumstances, you are unlikely to get the chance to confirm their story. You don't even have time for one last prayer...
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: You stand on the shore of Loch Calderwood, completely speechless at the picture presented to you: In front of you lies a picturesque mountain lake, surrounded by high, rugged mountains, behind which the sun is slowly setting. From the northwest you can hear a waterfall coming down from the mountains and tumbling loudly into the mountain lake. You feel the hint of a romantic feeling rising in you and consider calling your girlfriend for a moment - but at the same time you shy away from the thought: How should such a romantic have any chances with the girls here? And as for your girlfriend: After all, you didn't leave her at home without a reason, right? In this context, however, the thought occurs to you that a few laps in the lake would certainly do you good before you delight the Scottish ladies with your attention. So if you want to improve your physical condition before your campaign of conquest, you can enter the lake in the north. Otherwise, you can return to your hotel, which is at the end of the road heading south.
corrections.after: You stand on the shore of Loch Calderwood, speechless at the view. Before you lies a picturesque mountain lake, ringed by high, jagged peaks behind which the sun is slowly setting. To the northwest, a waterfall roars down from the mountains. A dangerously romantic feeling comes over you, and you consider calling your girlfriend. Then you dismiss the idea. What chance would a soppy romantic have with the girls around here? Besides, you left your girlfriend at home for a reason, didn't you? A few lengths of the lake might be just the thing to get you in shape before you bestow your attentions on the ladies of Scotland. If you'd like a little exercise before your campaign of conquest, enter the lake to the north. Otherwise, the road south leads back to your hotel.
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: When you enter the hotel's dining room, you have to smile: Compared to the number of guests who regularly book a room here every year, the room is a bit too big, almost as if it had been built for state banquets or other festive table delights : The candles in the precious stands on each table make it almost "first-class-look-a-like", but: what for? Usually the only guests who come here for dinner are the locals themselves! One of them, an older man with a long beard, is sitting at the table in the corner studying the menu while sipping his beer with relish. If the desire for food and drink has overcome you too, you can sit down with him. Otherwise you can exit the dining room through the door behind you.
corrections.after: You can't help smiling as you enter the hotel dining room. For the handful of guests who book rooms here each year, it's absurdly large, as though it were designed for state banquets. Candles in expensive holders on every table almost give it a first-class air. But why bother? Most of the diners are locals! One of them, an elderly man with a long beard, sits at a corner table studying the menu and savouring his beer. If you're hungry or thirsty, you could join him. Otherwise, you can leave through the door behind you.
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: As you wade west along the muddy shoreline, the water gets colder and colder - and, logically, deeper and deeper as you near the center of the lake. Until now it was still reasonably possible to stand on the bottom of the lake, but now you simply have no other choice: You have to swim if you don't want to sink! "So be it: Praised be what makes you hard!", you think to yourself, briefly sprinkle your hero's chest and then throw yourself forward with death defiance. Uahhh! Despite the warm season, the water is already quite cool, but after a few seconds you get used to the temperature. Actually quite pleasant here - only your rubber ducky is missing! As you make those first clumsy strokes, you also feel the strong current pulling you south, where a gigantic whirlpool is dragging into its deep maw anything careless enough to get within its reach. You can swim in all directions except west.
corrections.after: As you wade west across the muddy lake bed, the water gets colder and deeper. Until now you could just about stand, but you're running out of bottom. Time to swim, unless you fancy sinking! "Oh well, it'll toughen me up!" you tell yourself. You splash a little water onto your heroic chest, then fling yourself forwards with magnificent disregard for your own survival. Brrr! For a summer evening, that water is cold! After a few seconds you get used to it. Quite pleasant, really. All that's missing is your rubber duck. As you make your first clumsy strokes, you feel a strong current pulling you south, towards a gigantic whirlpool that swallows anything careless enough to stray within reach. You can swim in any direction except west.
corrections.reason: Toughening-up joke is about cold water, not sexual arousal; preserve all navigation directions.

corrections.before: You are standing in the cold water of the mountain lake. It's still pretty shallow, but the bottom feels pretty weird - maybe you're trampling on Nessie right now? Nevertheless: If you are not deterred by the cold water and the prospect of being able to serve a real monster as supper, you will probably get ahead without any problems. However, if you have changed your mind and wisely return to shore rather than play the hero, head south. However, if you don't want to listen to my advice, feel free to continue your way west - you'll see what you get out of it! But always remember: It was your idea...!
corrections.after: You are standing in the cold water of the mountain lake. It's still shallow, but the bottom feels rather odd. Perhaps you're treading on Nessie? If neither the temperature nor the prospect of becoming a monster's supper bothers you, you should have no trouble carrying on. If you've sensibly changed your mind about playing the hero, head south to the shore. Or ignore my advice and continue west. You'll find out soon enough! Just remember: this was YOUR idea...
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.after: [In the marketplace]

You can now either swim back to the center of the lake, or try to dive under the waterfall to see which one secret is hidden behind the opaque wall of water...
corrections.after: You are swimming in front of the waterfall at the northwest end of the lake. Struggling against the current, you wonder what might be behind that wall of water. You can swim back towards the middle of the lake, or try diving beneath the waterfall to discover what it hides...
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: Still dazed from the hard blow that the waterfall gave you, you try to keep yourself above the surface of the water with light, but still quite awkward swimming strokes, but suddenly you stop and stop - so that you can start again for a moment sink and swallow water! When you surface again, you get a shock: you seem to be still paddling on the southern side of the waterfall! Somehow a plausible explanation could even be found for this fact alone, especially since you had lost your bearings for a short time under water, so that you could accept it if, if... -if your village were still there on the lake shore ! But it seems to have disappeared from the face of the earth! Instead of the small settlement, there is a deep, dark forest on the shore with trees that you have never seen in your whole life! The suspicion arises in you that you might have gotten through the waterfall into a world that exists parallel to yours, like in those crazy adventures at home on your computer. Only: THIS is the reality! And where the hell did you end up here?
corrections.after: Still dazed by the waterfall's battering, you struggle to keep afloat. Then you freeze in astonishment, promptly sink and swallow a mouthful of water! When you surface, the shock hits you: you're still on the south side of the waterfall! That alone might have a perfectly reasonable explanation. You did lose your bearings underwater. You could accept it if... if... if the village were still there! But it has vanished. Where the little settlement stood, a deep, dark forest now crowds the shore, full of trees you've never seen before. Could the waterfall have brought you into a parallel world, like those daft adventures you play on your computer at home? Except THIS is real! Where the hell have you ended up?
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: You step onto the shore from where the rumble of the waterfall can still be heard in the southwest corner of the mountain lake. Nature somehow looks much cleaner and more untouched here than on the side from which you first entered the lake - you don't even know how long ago that was! Nevertheless, you're slowly beginning to like this world, although you don't know exactly where your parents will think you are if you don't call home tonight. However, it doesn't take a great deal of imagination to figure out that this would probably have been your last "solo vacation" until you came of age...
corrections.after: You climb onto the shore. The waterfall still rumbles in the southwest corner of the lake. Everything here seems cleaner and more untouched than on the side where you first entered the water. How long ago was that, anyway? Despite everything, you're beginning to like this world. You're less sure where your parents will imagine you are when you fail to call tonight. It doesn't take much imagination to work out that this is likely to be your last solo holiday until you're legally an adult...
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

But as I'm sure you can imagine, even a vulgar clearing like this has special meaning in an A.C.A adventure. And since you haven't solved the game yet, I would suggest you just wait it out!
corrections.after: You are at the edge of a clearing, surrounded by trees of a kind you don't recognise. There really isn't much else to say. Making up all those other room descriptions was hard enough! This place simply exists, just as you do. For the moment, anyway. Heh heh... Still, as you've probably guessed, even an ordinary clearing can serve a purpose in an A.C.A adventure. Since you're nowhere near finishing the game, I suggest you wait and see!

corrections.before: As you enter the clearing, you hear a terrible growling and hissing in front of you! Startled, you stop and hide behind the next tree to be on the safe side! When your eyes get used to the somewhat dim light, you see two animals fighting on the other side of the clearing: a large, gray wolf and a delicate, shimmering white unicorn, whose fur is already completely soiled with its bluish blood oozing from countless deep wounds. Noticing that the weakened unicorn's resistance is failing, the wolf attacks it even more furiously! The graceful mythical creature no longer has enough strength to resist the long, sharp wolf teeth for much longer...
corrections.after: As you enter the clearing, dreadful growls and snarls stop you in your tracks. You duck behind the nearest tree, just in case. As your eyes adjust to the gloom, you make out two animals fighting across the clearing: a large grey wolf and a slender, shimmering white unicorn. The unicorn's coat is soaked with bluish blood from countless deep wounds. Sensing its opponent weakening, the wolf attacks with renewed fury. The graceful creature cannot withstand those long, sharp teeth much longer...
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: Although you actually feel an urgent human need after the long journey, your curiosity wins and you decide to take a look at your new home first. You open the door expectantly and take a quick look around. Oh God! This is really bad... Everything is tiled - and it stinks here too! When you pull the cord to turn on the light, all you hear is a gurgling and smacking noise - and the light stays off! Can't deal with that! You storm towards the reception to give the old geezer of a doorman a good shout about what he means by a room with a shower, when the hammer drops! Plagued by foreboding, you go back to the door and carefully compare the number on the sign with the room number you were given: "003". The first digit is correct, the second too - but the third? Where the hell did the third digit go??? Holy crap! How are you supposed to find your way around here if these Scots are too thrifty to properly label their rooms? On your protest march to the reception you look at the signs on the other doors: "001", "002"... Hey! Wait a minute, then this should be... Yes, that's right: This is number "003"! At the very end of the aisle! You were just in the wrong room! All right, let's skip the trip to the porter and give him one more chance. But: WHERE THE HELL IS THE TOILET?!?!?
corrections.after: After the long journey, you urgently need the toilet, but curiosity wins: first, a look at your new home. You open the door expectantly. Oh, wonderful. What a load of sh... Everything is tiled, and the place stinks! You pull the cord to turn on the light. There's a gurgle and a slosh, but it stays dark. This is NOT on! You storm towards reception to give that old porter a piece of your mind about what "room with shower" is supposed to mean. Then the penny drops. With a sinking feeling, you return and compare the number on the door with your room number: "003". First digit, correct. Second digit, correct. Third digit... Where the hell is the third digit? Damn it! How is anyone meant to find their way around if these Scots are too stingy to number their rooms properly? On your way back to complain, you check the other doors: "001", "002"... Hang on. Then this must be... Yes! "003", right at the end of the corridor! You simply had the wrong room. Fine. Let's spare the porter and give him another chance. But WHERE THE HELL IS THE TOILET NOW?!?!?

corrections.before: You wave the waitress over to you and tell her your most urgent wishes: "Please bring me a large steak, a cold beer and the Fra..." - Suddenly you feel yourself blushing and stammer: "Oops: forget the Frankfurter Allgemeine. You probably don't get any German newspapers here anyway, right?" When the girl, also red up to her ears, hastily says no, you reassure her - deliberately ignoring the age difference of a good ten years - in a fatherly way: "It doesn't matter, my daughter: I can't speak German anyway!", and burst into a roar of laughter whereupon the villager, who had previously been sitting there uninvolved, rolled his eyes up to the sky in suffering, as if he had been kicked in the soft parts where it really hurt. When you realize with dismay that the waitress also appears to be suffering from a chronic lack of humor, you decide to abruptly stop your comic performance and dismiss the girl with a merciful wave of your hand. When she has disappeared into the kitchen, you ask the old man if he could tell you a little about the village and its surroundings. Slowly and surely, the villager begins to mumble into his beard that he can tell you an interesting legend. Well, you didn't exactly expect him to tell you the addresses of the local hot spots and yuppie discos, but does it have to be a fairy tale? As a precaution, you put your head on your hands so that in an emergency you don't hit your nose on the edge of the table, and while you wait longingly for your food, you at least have something to do, you listen to the old man's story: a long, long time ago a one time a rich and proud city was said to have stood where Loch Calderwood does - but in one single night it had disappeared and in its place was the lake at the foot of the mountains! It was believed that the inhabitants of this legendary city were punished by the gods for their pride and vanity. It is also said that they were very rich and artistic! Since you, for your part, have been practicing the art of sleeping with your eyes open since the beginning of the story, the local takes your stare for incredulous amazement and goes one step further: Apparently the people in the village still claim that even today the towers and roofs of the city could still be seen under water if one dared to dive down to the bottom of the lake under the full moon at midnight - a very exclusive and unique pleasure, by the way, since none of the brave men who have tried their luck so far have ever done so and came back...
corrections.after: You beckon the waitress over and announce your most pressing needs: "A big steak, a cold beer and a Fra..." Suddenly you blush. "Er, forget the Frankfurter Allgemeine. You probably don't get German newspapers here anyway, do you?" The girl, equally red-faced, hurriedly says no. Ignoring the good ten years between you, you reassure her in a fatherly tone: "Never mind, my child. I can't speak German anyway!" You roar with laughter. The local, who has been minding his own business, rolls his eyes as though your joke has caught him squarely between the legs. Discovering that the waitress also suffers from a chronic lack of humour, you cut your performance short and dismiss her with a gracious wave. Once she has disappeared into the kitchen, you ask the old man about the village and its surroundings. He slowly mumbles into his beard that he knows an interesting legend. Fine. You weren't expecting a list of trendy nightspots and yuppie discos, but does it have to be a fairy tale? You prop your head on your hands, just in case you nod off and hit your nose on the table. Longing for your food so you'll at least have something to do, you listen. Long ago, a rich, proud city stood where Loch Calderwood lies today. In a single night it vanished, leaving a lake at the foot of the mountains! People said the gods had punished its inhabitants for their pride and vanity. They were said to be wealthy and wonderfully skilled craftsmen. You've been practising the art of sleeping with your eyes open, but the old man mistakes your stare for amazement and goes one better. Even now, the villagers claim you can see the city's towers and rooftops if you dive to the bottom of the lake at midnight under a full moon. A very exclusive, once-in-a-lifetime experience, apparently. Not one of the brave men who tried it ever came back...
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: The old man hides his face behind his beer glass - unable to say another word. The only thing you still hear from him from time to time is a quiet and bashful "Börks!". Apparently he drank a glass over his thirst during his story...

corrections.before: After recovering a little, the unicorn thanks you for your help and strongly warns you to continue on your way west. "Once you have left this part of the forest, there is no turning back...", it says with an infinitely sad look in its deep blue eyes, "But take this little crystal ball: it could help you make friends in this hostile world..." With these words, the unicorn gives you a small, glowing crystal ball while whispering to you in a dying voice: "Think of me when you use it - I don't have long to live...". With one last look back at you, a look so full of regret and pain that it almost breaks your heart, the doomed beautiful creature turns and slowly trotts away without looking back at you until it is between the trees has disappeared...
corrections.after: After recovering a little, the unicorn thanks you and earnestly warns you against continuing west. "Once you leave this part of the forest, there is no turning back..." Its deep blue eyes are filled with sadness. "But take this little crystal ball. It may help you find friends in this hostile world..." It gives you the small, glowing ball and whispers in a fading voice, "Think of me when you use it. I do not have long to live..." The beautiful, doomed creature gives you one last look, so full of sorrow and pain that it almost breaks your heart. Then it turns and slowly walks away, never looking back, until it disappears among the trees...
corrections.reason: The unicorn warns against going west, not to go west; preserve no-return and friendship clues.

corrections.after: Still trembling from your narrow escape, you stop at the western edge of the bog to catch your breath. There's no sign of your pursuers. You've lost them! But where now? "Damn it!" you think bitterly. "Why didn't I stay in my cosy hotel and relax for a few weeks? I had to go looking for adventure, didn't I? Now look at me: stranded in the middle of nowhere with a pack of snapping zombies behind me! This whole game was a waste of money. I'll never buy rubbish like this again!" Just how right that last statement is becomes clear when you look around. The only way out is east, straight back to the zombies. They stopped chasing you for a reason: they know this bog very well. Sooner or later, it will be your grave...

corrections.before: As you walk across the moor on a more imaginary than actual path that runs south-west, your feet sink deeper and deeper into the spongy-soft ground. The impenetrable, damp fog that rises on both sides of your path, thickens into grotesque mythical creatures, the sight of which sends chills down your spine... A short time later, however, you tell yourself that everything that happens around you is just is a product of your overwrought nerves - pipe dreams that only grow from your fertile imagination. To give you a little encouragement, you think back to your previous adventures in this world, and that there's a little more to scaring Dave Parker than just a few ridiculous wisps of fog and a spooky background noise. You are just about to continue on your way with renewed courage when you hear a strange bubbling sound in front of you that seems to be getting closer and closer - a sound that is anything but unreal! You look around frantically, but nowhere in the middle of the waving sea of fog can you find an explanation for these eerie noises that seem to come straight from the deepest depths of the moor...
corrections.after: The path through the bog runs from south to west, though it owes more to your imagination than to anything underfoot. Your feet sink deeper into the spongy ground. Dense, damp mist rises on either side, taking the shapes of grotesque creatures that send shivers down your spine. Nonsense, you tell yourself. Just frayed nerves and an overactive imagination. After everything you've survived, it'll take more than a bit of fog and some spooky noises to frighten Dave Parker! You're about to press on with renewed courage when a strange bubbling noise comes from ahead, growing closer and closer. THAT is no figment of your imagination. You look around wildly, but the rolling fog hides the source of those dreadful sounds. They seem to rise from the deepest part of the bog...
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: You are right before the destination of your journey - the castle ruins of Zargon! If you dare, you can now attempt to enter Zargon's stronghold - but no one would blame you if, faced with the dangers lurking behind those walls, you backed out at the last moment and returned to your boat on the southern shore of the island.
corrections.after: Before you stands your destination: Zargon's ruined castle! Little remains of the former royal palace. The only intact structure among the sorry ruins is an enormous gateway in the high wall before you. Rather discouragingly, it seems to be the only way into Zargon's headquarters. You can try entering his stronghold, if you dare. Nobody would blame you for thinking better of it and returning to your boat on the southern shore, though. There are some very unpleasant things behind those walls...
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: You enter the gatehouse through which, long, long ago, anyone who wished to enter the king's palace had to pass. Nevertheless, I guess that the usual rabble got ahead of us and plundered everything that wasn't nailed down here long ago... Through the small door in the east wall you can get back outside, in front of the castle gate.
corrections.after: You enter the gatehouse through which everyone visiting the king's castle once had to pass. You chuckle at the thought of the deaf old "gatekeeper" from "Mary's Inn" sitting here, inspecting the visitors. A thick layer of dust covers everything. Even so, I suspect the usual rabble got here first and carried off anything that wasn't nailed down. A small door in the east wall leads back outside, to the castle gate.
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: The massive castle gate with its iron fittings rises threateningly and massively in front of you. It seems to be staring down at you maliciously - almost as if it wanted to say: "I will never let you out of here again...!", and promptly you get the light and vague, but on the other hand absolutely not pleasant feeling that You will actually only pass through this entrance to the castle once... You still have a little time to think carefully about your project - and we should warn you to be fair, although you are actually already on the right path to solving your task : If you actually dare to enter this gloomy building against all our warnings, this game will not let you sleep until you finally solve it. So I suggest that you start by brewing a few kegs of coffee, buy a few packs of cigarettes - and most importantly, come up with some reasonably intelligent excuses for your boss! So, after all these terrifying announcements, should you still have the courage - or the recklessness? - own the ability to enter Zargon's castle - here are the exits: To the west you'll find yourself in a small gatehouse where you might find a last-minute clue or useful item. On the other hand, if you go north, you either enter the interior of the ruins, or you slam into solid oak wood with full force - depending on the condition of the castle gate... Finally, you still have the option of retreating south, out of the castle - without your mission having fulfilled doesn't make a lot of sense, don't you think...?
corrections.after: The enormous, iron-bound castle gate looms before you. It seems to grin down maliciously: "You're never getting out again!" An unpleasant little feeling tells you that you may only pass through this entrance once. You still have time to reconsider. In fairness, we ought to warn you: although you're on the right track, once you enter this gloomy pile you won't sleep until you've finished the game. So brew a few barrels of coffee, buy a few cartons of cigarettes, and above all think up some convincing excuses for your boss! Still got the courage, or the poor judgement, to enter Zargon's castle? Here are the exits. West leads to a small gatehouse, where you might find a last-minute clue or useful object. North takes you into the ruins, or headfirst into solid oak, depending on whether the gate is open. You could also retreat south, away from the castle, though that won't do much to complete your mission, will it?
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: Hmmm...: While I'm well aware that there are people who appreciate a mud bath for its health benefits, this is a deep swamp - not just some harmless little bog! corrections.after: Hmm... I know some people swear by mud baths, but this is a deep swamp, not a harmless spa treatment! You sink helplessly to the bottom of the lake, where you'll be preserved for all eternity. Personally, I think preserving yourself with the "Save" command would have been rather healthier...
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: After a few meters you stop and listen again to the deceptive silence: No, it wasn't really your imagination - there are actually noises that stand out unpleasantly from the constant bubbling of the moorland! Footsteps are approaching you from behind, getting louder and louder - slowly but unstoppably... Startled, you whirl around, but can see nothing but dense, wafting wafts of fog, which twist into grotesque grimaces mocking you for your fear... Suddenly however, the ground next to you begins to seethe and bubble as if it were boiling - and then the horribly disfigured face of a half-decomposed corpse emerges from the depths! Frozen in horror and unable to take your eyes off the horrific spectacle, you watch as a zombie rises from the depths of the bog! The moment you regain control of yourself, its clawed claws will shoot for your throat! You don't know how, but somehow you throw yourself to the side again with all your strength and thus avoid certain death! However, you stumble during your parade and land hard in the mud! Now the Blackblood seems to have finally won: while you are struggling to get back on your feet, he hisses and hisses at you: as he staggers towards you, his jaws open and close with a creaking sound, exposing his disgustingly -brown tooth stumps...
corrections.after: After a few paces, you stop and listen to the deceptive silence. No, you weren't imagining it. Something is moving beneath the constant bubbling of the bog. Footsteps approach from behind, slow but relentless. You whirl round, but see only thick mist twisting into grotesque faces that seem to mock your fear. Suddenly the ground beside you begins to boil. A horribly disfigured face breaks the surface: a half-rotted corpse! Frozen with horror, you watch a zombie drag itself from the depths. As you regain control of your limbs, its claws shoot towards your throat! Somehow you fling yourself aside in time, but stumble and land hard in the mud. The undead creature seems to have won. While you struggle to your feet, it staggers closer, hissing and snarling. Its jaws creak open and shut, exposing the revolting brown stumps of its teeth...
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: I'm sorry: you really had a real chance to get away with the horror again, but unfortunately you hesitated a little too long again: happily the zombie pulls you towards you and happily sinks its teeth into your young, tender one Meat! But don't despair: at least until you fall victim to a true gourmet, and surely some of your tastiest body parts, such as your eyes, tongue, and similar delicacies, will be shipped off to his stash cave and canned, as it's just far too rare for a unfortunate adventurer strayed into this area, than one should eat such fat prey on the spot...
corrections.after: Sorry. You had a real chance to escape with nothing worse than a fright, but you hesitated too long. The delighted zombie pulls you close and sinks its teeth into your young, tender flesh! Still, don't despair. You've fallen victim to a true gourmet. Some of your tastier parts, eyes, tongue and similar delicacies, will doubtless be taken to its store-cave and preserved. Unfortunate adventurers stray out here far too rarely to waste such a feast in one sitting...
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

corrections.before: It was a fatal mistake to come back here after your earlier encounter: A veritable pack of zombies is already ready to receive you and is coming straight at you with slow, jerky movements and a fixed gaze - at the top is the zombie you just met narrowly escaped! This time, however, you have a little more control over yourself and your reaction is a lot faster than before: you spin around in a flash, grab your feet and run for your life as fast as you can on the soft moorland - and straight into the outstretched arms of another zombie who probably didn't quite get what was going on out here! Too bad, really - because your time was almost a world record! Nonetheless, the zombie is delighted to make your acquaintance, as it hasn't had fresh meat for weeks - and only eating "canned adventurers" that have sunk into the swamp is, in the long run, even for a half-rotted zombie stomach a somewhat one-sided and unhealthy diet! After a short prayer, he gratefully sinks his tusks into your flesh: "Damn! Who would have thought that these brown stumps could still be so sharp...", is your last thought before everything blurs before your eyes...
corrections.after: Coming back after your last encounter was a fatal mistake. A whole pack of zombies waits to welcome you, advancing with jerky movements and fixed stares. Leading them is the one you only just escaped! This time you react much faster. You spin round and run for your life as fast as the soggy ground allows, straight into the arms of another zombie who hadn't quite caught up with the proceedings. A shame, really. You were on course for a world record! Your new acquaintance is delighted. It hasn't had fresh meat in weeks, and a diet of bog-preserved adventurers gets a bit monotonous, even for a half-rotten stomach. After saying a quick grace, it gratefully sinks its teeth into you. "Damn! Who knew those brown stumps could still be so sharp?" is your last thought before everything blurs...
corrections.reason: Natural English, faithful meaning and the original cheeky narrator voice.

So you'd do very well to introduce yourself contacting me - I live here and...", he pauses in shock and looks at your hands, which are just practicing the most diverse choking movements, and then hastily continues: "Well, even at the risk that you You'll call me crazy" - you laugh hysterically - "I have to tell you that the rivers flow uphill here at midnight and at full moon all the adventurers the swamp has swallowed up over the decades rise from their damp graves and partying in hilarious orgies! "Yes, of course I know about the island! I've lived here for over ten years! Quite right to ask me. I live here, you see, and..." "Now, you may think me mad" - you laugh hysterically - "but at midnight the rivers here flow uphill! And under a full moon, all the adventurers swallowed by the swamp over the decades rise from their watery graves and hold wild orgies! Even Zargon, the Dark Lord himself, attends to review his undead palace guard. He once made a pact with the devil, who had his soul frozen and imprisoned in a huge magical crystal..." Just as a dense cloud of gray dust rises from the yellowing pages, you hear a bolt of lightning strike the main tower outside, sending the room into its ghostly for split seconds , pale light descends and the building shakes to its foundations - as if a gigantic, iron fist wanted to wipe out this hotbed of evil once and for all! corrections.after: You begin reading the tower guard's battered diary. It describes the siege from its first beginnings to its bitter end. The perceptive guard had noticed the disputes and power struggles between his master and Zargon long before King Richard could even imagine a coup. Yet even he could never have expected what was to come! Richard's ghost clearly wasn't exaggerating: while the king's body lay cold and twisted on the floor of Zargon's chamber, the sorcerer rounded up his former followers like cattle in the courtyard. There he offered them a choice: serve him, or follow their king into death. And there the diary ends... Cold anger cries out for revenge within you, mingled with desperate helplessness. You snap the little leather-bound book shut, unable to stare at that abrupt ending any longer. A thick grey cloud of dust rises from its yellowed pages. At that instant, lightning strikes the main tower outside, flooding the room with ghostly pale light for a fraction of a second and shaking the building to its foundations, as though a giant iron fist were trying to smash this nest of evil once and for all! It must have been much the same on the fateful night when the brave tower guard stood by his master for the very last time...

corrections.before: As you push down on the doorknob, you hear a faint click beneath your feet - and before you have time to jump back, a hidden trapdoor opens beneath you! At the last moment you grab the edge of the pitfall and try to pull yourself back up: "I wish I hadn't skipped gym class so often!", you think to yourself desperately when, after several futile and exhausting attempts, you realize that you are... you will never be able to free yourself from this predicament without outside help. When you look at the bottom of the pit in a panic, you see long iron spikes deep below you, with remnants of coagulated blood sticking to them! You instinctively want to call for help, but as soon as you open your mouth you realize that your screams would only be a complete waste of energy and time, since the only person who could hear and find you down here would be Zargon himself - and you know very well that he would have no pity on you! So after you have reminded yourself of the hopelessness of your situation, you say one last prayer and then let go of the edge of the pit... Well, a man has to know when it's time for him to go: Unfortunately, you fall You stay longer than expected and hit your head countless times on the hard, jagged rock faces, but without really losing consciousness - then it's suddenly over: impaled on the pointed lances, your wild death scream shakes the whole castle, one and only alone drowned out by Zargon's malicious sneers...
corrections.after: You push the door handle down. A faint click sounds beneath your feet, and before you can jump back, a hidden trapdoor opens! At the last instant you catch the edge of the pit and try to haul yourself up. "I wish I hadn't skipped so many PE lessons!" you think desperately. Several exhausting attempts later, you realise you'll never get out without help. Looking down in panic, you see long iron spikes far below, crusted with dried blood. You open your mouth to shout, then realise that would only waste your breath. The only person who could hear you down here is Zargon, and you know exactly how much sympathy you'd get from him! Facing the hopelessness of your position, you say one last prayer and let go. A man has to know when it's time to leave... Unfortunately, the drop lasts longer than expected. Your head strikes the jagged rock walls again and again, yet you never quite lose consciousness. Then, suddenly, it's over. Impaled on the spikes, you let out a dying scream that shakes the castle, drowned out only by Zargon's mocking laughter...
corrections.reason: Restore natural prose and consistently describe the fatal downward movement of a lever handle.

The Diary of the Tower Guardian
1st Day of the Year 713:
This morning, the couriers finally returned from the icy regions, where Firon, our King's brother, had
visited his palace to deliver New Year's blessings. However, none of them seemed particularly
pleased or hopeful. On the contrary, a message from the Elf King Firon seemed to have left them
quite frightened. That's all I could find out so far. Even King Richard appeared very worried when he
spoke with the envoy who left his meeting room!

2nd Day of the Year 713:
The beginning of the new year promises unfortunate events. An accident occurred today during the
hunt, in which the noble Sir Henryk's horse stumbled during the badger hunt, burying him
underneath. Sir Henryk was last seen, along with the old Archmage Grywinn and the king himself.
Grywinn had spoken out against the appointment of the young, ambitious court magician Zargon
into the Seventh Circle of the Mages Guild. Now, King Richard and Grywinn stand alone with their
opposition, while Zargon is getting closer to his goal. He has dedicated years to perfecting his
knowledge of magical elements, but he also possesses the strength of character and wisdom
necessary for the prosperity of our country. We don't know where he came from, as he has never
shared anything about himself with any of us. He is a secretive, mysterious individual, and I can't
help feeling uneasy about him.

3rd Day of the Year 713:
In the early hours of the morning, the country's nobles laid Sir Henryk to rest in the graveyard of the
St. Jacobi monastery. After the nobles returned from the funeral mass, a grand banquet was held in
honour of the deceased. To distract myself from my gloomy thoughts, I watched the young officers
and their ladies walking in the courtyard from my chamber on the main tower. The court servants
were busy, rushing around to ensure the guests lacked nothing. After Vyrtron relieved me for an
hour, I mingled with the guests to be part of the festivities.

Nobody noticed me, the lowly tower guard, among the elegantly dressed guests, so I had the
opportunity to observe undisturbed. Suddenly, I noticed a young girl hurrying past me, so beautiful
and graceful that I might have mistaken her for one of the noble ladies, if not for the white apron
she wore as a waitress. When she passed by again, I was still standing there, dumbstruck. She
blushed slightly and then gave me a happy wink before disappearing back into the kitchen. This
happened a few more times until I gathered the courage to hold her arm and ask her name. She
replied, "Simona." Unfortunately, I didn't have much time to talk to her, as she needed to attend to
the guests, and I had to return to my tower as my break was over. Before leaving, I whispered to
Simona to save some morsels from the feast and suggested that we meet shortly before midnight in
the castle basement for a private gathering. Now I'm sitting in my room, looking down at the
courtyard, counting the minutes until midnight. My only consolation until then is the opportunity to
admire Simona from my window. She spotted me and waved from below, laughing. It seems I'm not
entirely unsympathetic to her. I hope she truly comes tonight!

Simona did not disappoint me. Promptly, shortly before midnight, she entered the room on the
castle's lower floor. She did so quietly, and I was terribly startled when I suddenly saw her in front of
me. Although I was embarrassed by my reaction, she just smiled understandingly and pointed to a
basket of delicacies she had gathered from the remains of the feast. As we enjoyed good food and a

carafe of fine wine, we grew increasingly intimate, encouraged by the effect of the wine. Finally, I
confessed my love to her, and she replied with the words I had hoped to hear since our first
encounter. But suddenly, we heard soft footsteps on the stone spiral staircase leading back to the
entrance hall. To avoid compromising the young girl, I pulled her into a niche in the shadow of the
torches and hid beside her, curious to see who was interrupting our secret meeting. It was Zargon.
He slipped past us quietly and proceeded down the corridor until he stopped in front of a massive
door. He looked around hastily, pushed the door handle, and disappeared into the darkness behind
it. Still shocked by this mysterious turn of events, I wondered why Zargon was devoting himself to
his studies on this particular night. After all, he would be officially accepted into the Seventh Circle
of the Guild the next morning. He should be resting to be calm and composed on his significant day.
But why should we care about Zargon and his magical tricks when there are more important matters
to attend to?

4th Day of the Year 713:
As beautifully as yesterday ended, today was equally terrible. When Grywinn cast the runes to divine
the gods' judgment on Zargon's appointment as Archmage, a bolt of lightning struck from a clear sky
and turned Grywinn and his runewords into ashes. Panic ensued, and everyone was in disarray.
Zargon, however, remained composed. Standing next to Grywinn's charred remains, he took the
pentagram amulet meant for him and put it around his neck, declaring, "If the most powerful
magician in the country cannot choose me, the second most powerful must do it!" King Richard and
the terrified crowd were too stunned by the death of the wise Grywinn to oppose Zargon. Only King
Richard regarded him with disdain, revealing that he knew who was responsible for Grywinn's
demise. I caught a glimpse of Grywinn just before the lightning struck him. He appeared terrified by
what he had foreseen.

5th Day of the Year 713:
I am afraid. I can hardly sleep, haunted by the dread of what Grywinn may have foreseen. I fear that
Zargon, now that he has acquired magical power, might use it against his own people. He has already
shown that he values power over lives, but how cruel must his actions be to prepare for the murder
that has already taken place? Woe to us if my fears are confirmed.

Zargon's presence diminishes by the day, and when he does appear, it's often in the murky vaults of
the palace, where the king's ancestors rest. None of us common servants dare venture there alone.
If he notices that he is not alone, he hurries out of the room without a word of greeting, as though
he is fleeing from something. During my lunch break with Simona in the castle kitchen, we observed
a confrontation between Zargon and King Richard at the dining table. Zargon vehemently argued
that the country's army should be taught the basics of elemental magic to strengthen them, a
suggestion that Richard had rejected years ago. However, the power-hungry magician seemed to
have little respect for his ruler's decisions. He even called Richard a coward, accusing him of avoiding
thoughts of war. The dispute ended with King Richard angrily leaving the table, while Zargon sat
there with a sinister smile, playing with a table knife.

6th Day of the Year 713:
Something terrible has occurred! Noble warriors, should you read this one day, we are in grave
danger, and only the almighty gods can save our wretched souls. At midnight today, I heard screams
coming from the courtyard and rushed to the window to see what had happened. Horror gripped
me as I witnessed four half-decomposed mummies staggering through the courtyard. The great
castle gate swung open, and a horde of disfigured monsters stormed in, taking control of the royal
castle. Chaos ensued as the mob mercilessly slaughtered anyone who resisted. Then, an eerie silence

fell over the castle, and a procession of the undead emerged from the main building. Among them
was King Richard, offering no resistance as they led him to another part of the castle. After a moment
of silence, we heard my master's agonizing, prolonged death cry.

May the gods have mercy on my soul. In the courtyard, the surviving warriors of the king, driven
together like cattle for slaughter, now cower fearfully and tremble like children, fearing the worst.
Zargon, the treacherous traitor, the murderer and sinner, appears and leads the pack. He walks
slowly along the line of prisoners, then stands on a platform and presents them with a choice: to
serve him as their rightful master or follow their king in death. When none raise their hands to join
him, Zargon unleashes his henchmen on the helpless men, leading to a horrifying bloodbath that
claims the lives of all the castle residents.

Zargon has just ordered his minions to search the castle for any remaining survivors. It is only a
matter of time before they find me up here and descend to capture me. So, noble warriors, take this
book as the last testament to the glorious and peaceful times before evil descended upon our land.
Pray for our souls and avenge us, our friends, and our families. I hope I will have a chance to end my
own life, sparing myself the torments suffered by my fellow comrades.

1st Day of the Year 713:

This morning the couriers finally returned from the frozen lands. They had visited Firon, our king's brother, in his palace to deliver the king's blessings for the new year. Yet none of them looked pleased or hopeful. Quite the opposite: some message from Firon, the Elven King, must have frightened them badly. I have been unable to discover more, but even King Richard looked deeply troubled as he left his council chamber with the envoys.

2nd Day of the Year 713:

The new year begins with an ill omen. The noble Sir Henryk was killed on today's hunt when his horse stumbled during the pursuit of a badger and fell on top of him. Apart from the old Archmage Grywinn and the king himself, Sir Henryk was the last person at court to oppose admitting the young, ambitious court magician Zargon to the Seventh Circle of the Mages' Guild. Now the king and Grywinn stand alone against the other three archmages, and Zargon is close to his goal.

For years he has shut himself away to perfect his knowledge of the magical elements, but does he also possess the strength of character and wisdom needed to use that knowledge for the good of our people? We do not even know where he comes from. He has never spoken to any of us about himself. He is secretive and mysterious, and something about him frightens me.

3rd Day of the Year 713:

Early this morning, the nobles of the realm laid Sir Henryk to rest in the graveyard of St Jacobi's monastery. After they returned from the funeral service, a great banquet was held in his honour. To take my mind off these dark thoughts, I looked down from my chamber in the main tower at the young officers strolling through the courtyard with their sweethearts. Servants hurried to and fro, bringing this guest one thing and that guest another, determined that the king's company should want for nothing. When Vyrton relieved me for an hour, I went down to join them.

No one noticed a lowly tower guard among all those finely dressed guests, so I could watch undisturbed. Then a young woman hurried past, so beautiful and graceful that, but for her serving apron, I would have taken her for a noblewoman. I must still have been standing there thunderstruck when she came back. She blushed, gave me a cheerful wink and vanished into the kitchen. After this had happened two or three times, I finally plucked up the courage to catch her arm and ask her name. "Simona," she said.

There was no time to talk. She had guests to attend to, and my break was over. But before I left, Simona whispered to me that she had put aside a few treats from the feast. If I wished, I could meet her in the castle basement just before midnight, and we could have a little feast of our own. Now I sit here looking down into the courtyard and counting the minutes. My only consolation is that I can admire Simona from my window as much as I please. She has just spotted me and waved up, laughing. It seems she rather likes me too. I do hope she comes tonight!

Simona did not disappoint me. Just before midnight, she slipped into the basement so quietly that I jumped when she suddenly appeared before me. I was mortified, but she merely smiled and pointed conspiratorially to a basket of delicacies rescued from the banquet. Over good food and a carafe of rich wine, we grew ever closer — whether through the wine's charms or fate's designs, I cannot say. At last, emboldened by the wine, I confessed my love. She had just begun to say the words I had longed to hear since our first meeting when we heard soft footsteps on the stone spiral staircase leading to the entrance hall.

To protect her reputation, I drew her into a recess beyond the torchlight and hid beside her to see who had dared interrupt our secret meeting. It was Zargon! He crept past us and along the corridor, stopping at a heavy door. After a hurried glance over his shoulder, he pushed the door handle upwards and disappeared into the darkness beyond.

Still shaken by this strange interruption, I wondered why he would be studying tonight of all nights. Tomorrow he would enter the Seventh Circle of the Guild and fulfil his greatest ambition. Surely he ought to be asleep, ready to face his great day with a clear head. But what did we care about Zargon and his ridiculous conjuring tricks? There were more important things to attend to...

4th Day of the Year 713:

Yesterday ended so beautifully. Today was terrible. Before Zargon's initiation, Grywinn cast the rune-sticks to seek the gods' judgement on his elevation to archmage. Suddenly, a bolt of lightning struck from a clear sky and reduced Grywinn and his rune-sticks to ashes. Screams broke out. People fled in every direction. Only Zargon remained calm.

Standing tall beside Grywinn's charred body, he took the pentagram amulet intended for his initiation and hung it around his own neck. "If the most powerful magician in the land can no longer appoint me, then the second most powerful will have to do it!" he cried.

The king and the terrified crowd were too stunned by the old mage's death to protest. Richard alone looked at Zargon with open contempt, making it plain that he knew who was responsible. I saw Grywinn's face just before the lightning struck. Whatever he had seen in the future had filled him with terror...

5th Day of the Year 713:

I am afraid. I can scarcely sleep for fear of what Grywinn foresaw. Now that Zargon can wield the full extent of his magic, will he turn it against his own people? Yesterday proved that he will kill to gain power. What terrible deed can he be preparing, if even its preparation demands a murder? Woe to us if my fears prove true!

Zargon is seen less and less. When he does appear, it is often in the gloomy vaults where the king's ancestors lie buried — a place none of us ordinary servants would dare enter alone. If he notices anyone else there, he hurries out without a word, almost as though fleeing something.

While I sat with Simona in the castle kitchen during my midday break, we could see into the dining hall. Zargon was arguing fiercely with King Richard. He wanted the army taught the rudiments of magic to make it stronger, a proposal Richard had rejected years ago. The power-hungry magician seemed to have lost all respect for his ruler's decisions. He even called Richard a coward who was not man enough to contemplate war. At last the king rose in anger and strode out. Zargon remained at the table, smiling to himself and toying with his dinner knife...

6th Day of the Year 713:

Something dreadful has happened! Noble warrior, if you should one day read these words, know that we are in mortal danger. Only the almighty gods can save our poor souls now. At the stroke of midnight, I heard shouting in the courtyard and hurried to the window. Horror seized me. Four half-rotted mummies were staggering across the courtyard to open the great castle gate. It had barely opened a crack before a vast army of hideously disfigured monsters poured in and seized the castle.

Screams and cries filled the halls as the raging horde cut down everyone who resisted. Then all fell silent. A small band of rotting corpses, raised into a hideous mockery of life, emerged from the main building. In their midst was King Richard. He offered no resistance as they dragged him into another building. A few seconds of silence — then my lord's long, agonised death cry!

May the gods have mercy on my soul. The king's surviving soldiers have been herded into the courtyard like cattle for slaughter. They huddle together, trembling like frightened children. Now Zargon emerges from the doorway through which we heard our master's final cry: that wretched traitor, murderer and blasphemer! Slowly he walks along the line of prisoners, then steps onto a ledge. He offers the murdered king's followers a choice: serve Zargon as their rightful lord, or follow their king in death.

Not one man raises a hand to join him. Zargon unleashes his pack on the defenceless prisoners. Within moments, the courtyard becomes a slaughterhouse. None of them survives...

Zargon has just ordered his henchmen to search the castle for anyone still alive. It is only a matter of time before they find me up here and drag me down.
